title: Fukushima — 福島
goal: Expand food compounds and make a clear noun request.

cards.title: A Familiar Shopping Scene, More Useful Words

blocks.text: Fukushima is both a prefecture and its capital city. The city's surrounding orchard/fruit context appears in the official prefectural travel material. We will use an invented menu and shop conversation; no seasonal availability or real price is implied.
**福島で果物を買います。** ふくしまで くだものを かいます。 — I buy fruit in Fukushima.

果物 is introduced as a whole word now and unpacked below. This is not a predictable reading produced by adding standalone kanji sounds. Shopping and eating grammar are already available, so new nouns can quickly become useful.

items: **Character:** 福 · **Meaning/reading:** good fortune; フク · **Radical/components:** 示 in 礻/しめすへん form, beside 畐, a historical sound component; 畐 visibly includes 一/口/田-like sections · **Role:** Encounter. The right pieces do not simply sum to good fortune.
**Character:** 島 · **Meaning/reading:** island; しま, トウ · **Radical/components:** 山, やま; abbreviated bird-related upper shape · **Role:** Encounter review from 松島.

blocks.text: **福島 / ふくしま**. A name containing 島 does not make the city a separate island. Compare 松島 and 福島 to recognise the shared character while keeping different locations. The shrine-related 礻 differs from clothing radical 衤: the extra stroke can matter in another character family.

**茶 / ちゃ — tea; お茶 / おちゃ — tea with a common polite prefix.** Radical **艹**, くさかんむり, above a person-like middle and tree-like lower section. The plant top is useful; the lower strokes are recognition shapes rather than a formula “person plus tree = tea.”
**お茶を飲みます。** おちゃを のみます。 — I drink tea.
**お茶は飲み物です。** おちゃは のみものです。 — Tea is a drink.
お茶 and 茶 share the same central word. Do not count the prefix as a separate new kanji reading. This word directly enriches 飲む and 飲み物 from earlier packages.

**肉 / にく — meat; 牛肉 / ぎゅうにく — beef, explained next.** 肉 is its own radical, にく. Its modern enclosed shape has inner strokes; compare carefully with **内** rather than assume that every enclosed 人-like form is the same character. In other characters a flesh-related side component often resembles 月, but that wider family is a later recognition connection.
**肉を食べます。** にくを たべます。 — I eat meat.
**この肉は食べ物です。** この にくは たべものです。 — This meat is food.
These are category/action examples. The lesson does not require any learner to eat a particular food; other taught food nouns can occupy the same pattern.
**牛 / うし — cow/cattle; 牛肉 / ぎゅうにく — beef.** 牛 is its own radical, うし. The whole horn/head-derived shape becomes **牜**, うしへん, at the left of 物, which you already studied in Akita.
**これは牛です。** これは うしです。 — This is a cow, in a labelled illustration.
**牛肉を食べました。** ぎゅうにくを たべました。 — I ate beef.
The standalone animal is うし; the compound uses ぎゅう. Do not construct **うしにく** as the required ordinary beef word. The word 牛肉 names meat, not a live cow; a living cow in an existence scene uses います.
**果物 / くだもの — fruit.** 果 is indexed under **木**, き. Its modern upper 田-like section above 木 helps recognition and relates to a fruit/tree image; do not interpret it as a rice paddy growing on a tree.
**りんごは果物です。** りんごは くだものです。 — Apples are fruit.
**果物を二つ買いました。** くだものを ふたつ かいました。 — I bought two pieces/items of fruit, in a scene with whole fruits.
果 contributes **くだ** in this whole word; 物 is もの. Learn くだもの directly. It differs from 食べ物 / たべもの and 飲み物 / のみもの, whose verb stems are visible.

items: **Word:** ご飯 · **Reading:** ごはん · **Role/meaning:** review: rice/meal
**Word:** 魚 · **Reading:** さかな · **Role/meaning:** review: fish
**Word:** 牛肉 · **Reading:** ぎゅうにく · **Role/meaning:** core new word: beef
**Word:** 鶏肉 · **Reading:** とりにく · **Role/meaning:** assisted chicken-meat word; 鶏 remains encounter
**Word:** 野菜 · **Reading:** やさい · **Role/meaning:** assisted vegetable word; 野/菜 remain encounters
**Word:** 果物 · **Reading:** くだもの · **Role/meaning:** core new word: fruit
**Word:** お茶 · **Reading:** おちゃ · **Role/meaning:** core new word: tea

blocks.text: 鳥 / とり is bird; **鶏肉** uses a different first kanji for chicken. Do not teach **鳥肉** as the default spelling of the syllabus chicken word. The menu broadens usable vocabulary while formal kanji assignments stay limited.

cards.title: ください after a Noun

blocks.text: **お茶をください。** おちゃを ください。 — Tea, please / Please give me tea.
**りんごを二つください。** りんごを ふたつ ください。 — Two apples, please.

The taught pattern is **noun を (count) ください**, a polite request for an item. This is not yet **verb て-form + ください** for asking someone to perform an action. No new verb-conjugation rule is needed for the noun request.

We preserve を, which marks the requested item. A contextually supplied serving of tea can be requested without introducing a special cup counter. Use the existing general counter for stated whole apples.

cards.title: A Shop Conversation with a Total

blocks.text: **すみません。りんごを二つください。** すみません。りんごを ふたつ ください。 — Excuse me. Two apples, please.
**三百円です。** さんびゃくえんです。 — It is 300 yen, the stated total for both apples.
**ありがとうございます。** ありがとうございます。 — Thank you.
**食べ物と飲み物を買いました。** たべものと のみものを かいました。 — I bought food and drinks.

The scene also includes a drink, named in the accompanying practice menu. A total-price statement should not be confused with a per-item label. Questions later explicitly identify which quantity they ask about.
**米を買います。ご飯を食べます。お茶を飲みます。果物を買います。** こめを かいます。ごはんを たべます。おちゃを のみます。くだものを かいます。 — I buy uncooked rice. I eat cooked rice/a meal. I drink tea. I buy fruit.

These short sentences reuse the same object particle with different natural actions. The kanji graph connects **食 → 飯/食べ物**, **飲 → 飲み物**, **物 → 果物**, and **牛 → 牜 in 物**. A useful connection need not imply that every shared component has the same role in every word.

items: Read 福島, お茶, 牛肉 and 果物. **Answer:** ふくしま; おちゃ; ぎゅうにく; くだもの.
What radical links 果 with 林? **Answer:** 木.
Which is the ordinary standalone cow word? **Answer:** 牛 / うし.
Ask for two apples in the taught pattern. **Answer:** りんごを二つください。
Is お茶 a food noun or an action verb? **Answer:** a drink/item noun; 飲む is the action.
What first kanji is used in the assisted chicken-meat word? **Answer:** 鶏 in 鶏肉, rather than treating 鳥 as the default spelling.

blocks.text: 福島 is ふくしま; its 島 does not classify the city as an island. お茶 is tea; 肉 is meat; 牛 is うし and 牛肉 is ぎゅうにく. 果物 is くだもの. Request an item with **Nをください**, or a stated general count with **Nを二つください**. Keep menu encounters assisted.
**Recall task:** “Tea, please.” **Model:** お茶をください。 Continue to Aizuwakamatsu and identify the people in a family story.
